category: Aerospace Toolbox > Atmosphere & Environment, Rotations & Quaternions, Coordinate Frames, Orbits, Flight Parameters & Aircraft
description: Aerospace Toolbox functions for standard atmosphere, gravity, geomagnetic and ephemeris models; Euler angle/DCM/quaternion conversions and quaternion math; geodetic, ECEF, ECI and flat-Earth coordinate transformations; orbit elements and propagation; airspeed and flow relations; unit conversions; fixed-wing aircraft modeling and trajectory animation.

tools.name: atmoscoesa
tools.description: Computes temperature, speed of sound, pressure and density versus geometric altitude using the 1976 COESA (U.S. Standard Atmosphere) model. It is the reference atmosphere for flight simulation and performance calculations up to about 84.85 km.
tools.usage:
[T, a, P, rho] = atmoscoesa(height)
[T, a, P, rho] = atmoscoesa(height, action)
tools.notes: Outputs in K, m/s, Pa and kg/m^3. Use atmosisa for the ISA (0-20 km, faster), atmosnrlmsise00 for the upper atmosphere, and atmosnonstd for hot/cold day profiles.

tools.name: atmosisa
tools.description: Implements the International Standard Atmosphere model, returning temperature, speed of sound, pressure and density for altitudes in the troposphere and lower stratosphere. A quick standard-day model for aircraft performance.
tools.usage:
[T, a, P, rho] = atmosisa(height)
[T, a, P, rho] = atmosisa(height, Name=Value)
tools.example:
[T, a, P, rho] = atmosisa(11000)    % tropopause
mach = machnumber([230 0 0], a)
tools.notes: Valid from 0 to 20000 m (values are held beyond the limits). atmoslapse lets you specify custom lapse rates and base conditions.

tools.name: atmosnrlmsise00
tools.description: Implements the NRLMSISE-00 empirical model of the neutral atmosphere from the ground to the exosphere, returning temperatures and species number densities plus total mass density. Used for satellite drag and upper-atmosphere studies.
tools.usage:
[T, rho] = atmosnrlmsise00(altitude, latitude, longitude, year, dayOfYear, UTseconds)
[T, rho] = atmosnrlmsise00(___, f107Average, f107Daily, magneticIndex)
[T, rho] = atmosnrlmsise00(___, flags, iType, action)

parameters.name: f107Average, f107Daily, magneticIndex
parameters.description: Solar flux and geomagnetic activity indices (from space weather data).

tools.notes: T has exospheric and local temperature columns; rho has 9 columns (He, O, N2, O2, Ar, total mass density, H, N, anomalous O). Get indices with aeroReadSpaceWeatherData and fluxSolarAndGeomagnetic.

tools.name: atmoslapse
tools.description: Implements a lapse-rate atmosphere with user-specified gravity, gas properties, lapse rate, tropopause heights and sea-level conditions. Use it to model non-standard days or other planets' atmospheres.
tools.usage: [T, a, P, rho] = atmoslapse(height, g, heatRatio, characteristicGasConstant, lapseRate, heightTroposphere, heightTropopause, density0, pressure0, temperature0)

parameters.name: g / heatRatio / characteristicGasConstant
parameters.description: Gravity (m/s^2), specific heat ratio and gas constant (J/(kg K)).

parameters.name: heightTroposphere / heightTropopause
parameters.description: Top of troposphere and of tropopause (m).

tools.notes: Equivalent to ISA when standard values are used. atmosnonstd gives MIL-STD-210/MIL-HDBK-310 climatic profiles.

tools.name: atmospalt
tools.description: Computes pressure altitude from ambient static pressure using the standard atmosphere relation, as used by barometric altimeters.
tools.usage:
pressureAltitude = atmospalt(pressure)
pressureAltitude = atmospalt(pressure, action)
tools.notes: Valid roughly from 0.3961 Pa to 101325 Pa (standard atmosphere range).

tools.name: wrldmagm
tools.description: Computes the Earth's magnetic field vector, horizontal intensity, declination, inclination and total intensity with the World Magnetic Model at a given location, altitude and decimal year. Used for heading references and magnetometer simulation.
tools.usage:
[XYZ, H, D, I, F] = wrldmagm(height, lat, lon, dyear)
[XYZ, H, D, I, F] = wrldmagm(height, lat, lon, dyear, model)

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Altitude above WGS84 ellipsoid in meters.

parameters.name: lat, lon
parameters.description: Geodetic latitude and longitude in degrees.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: WMM epoch such as "2020" or "2025" (valid for 5 years).

tools.example:
[XYZ, H, D, I, F] = wrldmagm(0, 45.5, -73.6, decyear(2025, 7, 1));
fprintf("Declination %.2f deg, total field %.0f nT\n", D, F)
tools.notes: XYZ is in nanotesla in the north-east-down frame. igrfmagm implements the IGRF model with longer historical coverage.

tools.name: igrfmagm
tools.description: Calculates the Earth's magnetic field using the International Geomagnetic Reference Field, which covers historical dates back to 1900 as well as current epochs.
tools.usage:
[XYZ, H, D, I, F, dXYZ, dH, dD, dI, dF] = igrfmagm(height, lat, lon, dyear)
[___] = igrfmagm(height, lat, lon, dyear, generation)

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description: IGRF generation number (e.g. 13 or 14, depending on release).

tools.notes: Additional outputs give secular variation (nT/year, deg/year).

tools.name: gravitywgs84
tools.description: Computes Earth's gravity with the WGS84 ellipsoidal model, using a Taylor series, close approximation or exact method, optionally returning north and down components and including/excluding centrifugal effects.
tools.usage:
g = gravitywgs84(h, lat)
g = gravitywgs84(h, lat, lon, method, [noatm, nocent, prec, dyear], action)
[gn, gt] = gravitywgs84(___)
tools.notes: gravitysphericalharmonic provides high-degree geopotential models (EGM2008, EGM96) and other planets; gravityzonal uses zonal harmonics only.

tools.name: gravitysphericalharmonic
tools.description: Computes the gravity vector from a spherical harmonic planetary geopotential model (e.g. EGM2008, EGM96, lunar and Martian models) at positions given in planet-centered planet-fixed coordinates.
tools.usage:
[gx, gy, gz] = gravitysphericalharmonic(planetCoordinates)
[gx, gy, gz] = gravitysphericalharmonic(planetCoordinates, model)
[gx, gy, gz] = gravitysphericalharmonic(planetCoordinates, model, degree, action)
tools.notes: High degrees are slow; EGM2008 data may require aeroDataPackage. Output in m/s^2.

tools.name: geoidheight
tools.description: Calculates the geoid height (undulation between the geoid and the WGS84 ellipsoid) at given geodetic coordinates, used to convert between ellipsoidal (GPS) heights and mean-sea-level altitudes.
tools.usage:
N = geoidheight(lat, lon)
N = geoidheight(lat, lon, modelname)
N = geoidheight(___, action)
tools.example:
N = geoidheight(46.2, 7.5)          % meters
hMSL = hEllipsoid - N;
tools.notes: geoidegm96 is the EGM96-specific function. Larger models need the aerospace data package.

tools.name: planetEphemeris
tools.description: Returns the position and velocity of a target body (planets, Moon, Sun, Earth-Moon barycenter) relative to a center body at given Julian dates, from JPL Development Ephemerides.
tools.usage:
[position, velocity] = planetEphemeris(ephemerisTime, center, target)
[position, velocity] = planetEphemeris(ephemerisTime, center, target, ephemerisModel, units, action)
tools.notes: Ephemeris data is installed with aeroDataPackage. Frame is ICRF.

tools.name: angle2dcm
tools.description: Converts three rotation angles in a chosen sequence (default ZYX, i.e. yaw-pitch-roll) into a direction cosine matrix. The DCM transforms vectors from the reference frame into the rotated (body) frame.
tools.usage:
dcm = angle2dcm(r1, r2, r3)
dcm = angle2dcm(r1, r2, r3, S)

parameters.name: r1, r2, r3
parameters.description: Rotation angles in radians (m-by-1 arrays for multiple DCMs).

tools.notes: Returns 3-by-3-by-m arrays. Inverse: dcm2angle. For quaternions use angle2quat; Robotics/Navigation toolboxes use eul2rotm with different frame conventions.

tools.name: dcm2angle
tools.description: Extracts three rotation angles in a given sequence from a direction cosine matrix. Used to recover yaw, pitch and roll from attitude matrices.
tools.usage:
[r1, r2, r3] = dcm2angle(dcm)
[r1, r2, r3] = dcm2angle(dcm, S)
[r1, r2, r3] = dcm2angle(dcm, S, lim, action, tolerance)

parameters.name: action / tolerance
parameters.description: Validation of orthogonality of the DCM.

tools.notes: Euler angles are singular at pitch = +/-90 deg for ZYX; prefer quaternions for continuous attitude propagation.

tools.name: angle2quat
tools.description: Converts rotation angles in a given sequence to a unit quaternion in scalar-first [w x y z] form, the Aerospace Toolbox convention used by the quat* functions.
tools.usage:
q = angle2quat(r1, r2, r3)
q = angle2quat(r1, r2, r3, S)
tools.notes: Aerospace Toolbox quaternions are m-by-4 double arrays, not the quaternion class of Sensor Fusion/Navigation toolboxes (convert with quaternion(q)).

tools.name: quat2angle
tools.description: Converts scalar-first quaternions to rotation angles in a specified sequence, for example to display yaw/pitch/roll of an attitude estimate.
tools.usage:
[r1, r2, r3] = quat2angle(q)
[r1, r2, r3] = quat2angle(q, S)
tools.notes: Normalize quaternions before conversion; results are in radians.

tools.name: quat2dcm
tools.description: Converts quaternions to direction cosine matrices. Handy for transforming vectors with matrix multiplication or feeding DCM-based algorithms.
tools.usage: dcm = quat2dcm(q)
tools.notes: dcm2quat is the inverse. The DCM corresponds to a frame (passive) rotation, consistent with quatrotate.

tools.name: dcm2quat
tools.description: Converts direction cosine matrices to scalar-first quaternions, validating orthonormality within a tolerance.
tools.usage:
q = dcm2quat(dcm)
q = dcm2quat(dcm, action, tolerance)

parameters.name: action / tolerance
parameters.description: Behavior when the DCM is not orthonormal ("None", "Warning", "Error").

tools.notes: Related Euler-Rodrigues conversions: dcm2rod, rod2dcm, quat2rod, rod2quat.

tools.name: quatmultiply
tools.description: Computes the Hamilton product of two quaternions (or arrays of quaternions), which composes rotations. The order matters: quatmultiply(q, r) applies rotation r followed by q in the frame-rotation sense.
tools.usage: n = quatmultiply(q, r)
tools.notes: Other quaternion math: quatconj, quatinv, quatdivide, quatnormalize, quatnorm, quatmod, quatexp, quatlog, quatpower.

tools.name: quatrotate
tools.description: Rotates 3-D vectors by quaternions, returning the vectors expressed in the rotated frame (a coordinate/frame transformation, equivalent to quat2dcm(q)*v).
tools.usage: n = quatrotate(q, r)
tools.example:
q = angle2quat(pi/2, 0, 0);            % 90 deg yaw
v_body = quatrotate(q, [1 0 0])         % [0 -1 0]: NED x-axis seen from body
tools.notes: This is a passive (frame) rotation; to rotate a point actively use quatrotate(quatconj(q), r). Normalize q first.

tools.name: quatinterp
tools.description: Interpolates between two quaternions by a fraction f using spherical linear (SLERP), linear (LERP) or normalized linear (NLERP) interpolation. Useful for attitude animation and resampling.
tools.usage:
qi = quatinterp(p, q, f)
qi = quatinterp(p, q, f, method)
tools.notes: SLERP gives constant angular velocity; NLERP is cheaper and close for small steps.

tools.name: dcmecef2ned
tools.description: Computes the direction cosine matrix that transforms vectors from Earth-centered Earth-fixed (ECEF) axes to local north-east-down (NED) axes at a given geodetic latitude and longitude.
tools.usage: dcm = dcmecef2ned(lat, lon)

parameters.name: lat, lon
parameters.description: Geodetic latitude and longitude in degrees.

tools.notes: dcm2latlon recovers latitude/longitude from the DCM. For position conversion use lla2ecef/ecef2lla.

tools.name: dcmbody2wind
tools.description: Builds the direction cosine matrix from body axes to wind axes given angle of attack and sideslip angle, used to resolve aerodynamic forces (lift, drag, side force) between frames.
tools.usage: dcm = dcmbody2wind(alpha, beta)

parameters.name: alpha, beta
parameters.description: Angle of attack and sideslip in radians.

tools.example:
C_wb = dcmbody2wind(deg2rad(4), deg2rad(1));
F_wind = C_wb * F_body;     % [ -D; Y; -L ] components
tools.notes: dcm2alphabeta performs the inverse; dcmbody2stability gives the stability-axis transformation. alphabeta computes the angles from body velocities.

tools.name: lla2ecef
tools.description: Converts geodetic latitude, longitude and altitude to Earth-centered Earth-fixed Cartesian coordinates for the WGS84 or a custom ellipsoid.
tools.usage:
p = lla2ecef(lla)
p = lla2ecef(lla, model)
p = lla2ecef(lla, flattening, equatorialRadius)

parameters.name: lla
parameters.description: m-by-3 [lat lon alt] in degrees and meters.

tools.notes: ecef2lla is the inverse. Mapping Toolbox geodetic2ecef offers similar functionality with referenceEllipsoid objects.

tools.name: ecef2lla
tools.description: Converts Earth-centered Earth-fixed coordinates to geodetic latitude, longitude and altitude.
tools.usage:
lla = ecef2lla(p)
lla = ecef2lla(p, model)
lla = ecef2lla(p, flattening, equatorialRadius)
tools.notes: Altitude is above the ellipsoid, not MSL; subtract geoidheight for orthometric altitude.

tools.name: lla2flat
tools.description: Converts geodetic coordinates to flat-Earth (local tangent plane) position relative to a reference point and heading, a standard approximation for short-range flight simulation.
tools.usage:
flatearth_pos = lla2flat(lla, llo, psio, href)
flatearth_pos = lla2flat(lla, llo, psio, href, ellipsoidModel)

parameters.name: llo
parameters.description: Reference [lat lon] of the origin in degrees.

parameters.name: psio
parameters.description: Angle (deg) between flat-Earth x-axis and north.

tools.notes: flat2lla is the inverse. Accuracy degrades with distance from the origin.

tools.name: lla2eci
tools.description: Converts geodetic coordinates to Earth-centered inertial (ECI) position at a given UTC time, accounting for Earth rotation, precession and nutation.
tools.usage:
position = lla2eci(lla, utc)
position = lla2eci(lla, utc, reduction, deltaAT, deltaUT1, polarmotion)
tools.notes: eci2lla, eci2ecef, ecef2eci and dcmeci2ecef cover other directions.

tools.name: eci2ecef
tools.description: Transforms position, velocity and acceleration vectors from the Earth-centered inertial frame to Earth-centered Earth-fixed coordinates at a given UTC time.
tools.usage:
[r_ecef, v_ecef, a_ecef] = eci2ecef(utc, r_eci)
[r_ecef, v_ecef, a_ecef] = eci2ecef(utc, r_eci, v_eci, a_eci)
[___] = eci2ecef(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: utc
parameters.description: [year month day hour minute second] or datetime.

tools.notes: Name-value options set IERS corrections (dAT, dUT1, polar motion). ecef2eci is the inverse.

tools.name: keplerian2ijk
tools.description: Computes position and velocity vectors in an inertial (IJK) frame from classical Keplerian orbital elements, including special cases for circular and equatorial orbits.
tools.usage:
[r, v] = keplerian2ijk(a, ecc, incl, RAAN, argp, nu)
[r, v] = keplerian2ijk(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: ecc, incl, RAAN, argp, nu
parameters.description: Eccentricity, inclination, right ascension of ascending node, argument of periapsis and true anomaly (degrees).

parameters.name: truelon / arglat / lonper
parameters.description: Alternative angles for circular or equatorial orbits.

tools.notes: ijk2keplerian is the inverse. Gravitational parameter defaults to Earth's.

tools.name: ijk2keplerian
tools.description: Computes classical Keplerian orbital elements from inertial position and velocity vectors, returning also true longitude, argument of latitude and longitude of periapsis for degenerate orbits.
tools.usage: [a, ecc, incl, RAAN, argp, nu, truelon, arglat, lonper] = ijk2keplerian(r_ijk, v_ijk)
tools.notes: Angles are in degrees. NaN is returned for undefined elements (e.g. RAAN for equatorial orbits).

tools.name: propagateOrbit
tools.description: Propagates spacecraft orbits to given times from TLE/OMM structures, Keplerian elements or position/velocity states using two-body Keplerian, SGP4/SDP4 or numerical propagators, without creating a satellite scenario.
tools.usage:
[positions, velocities] = propagateOrbit(time, gpStruct)
[positions, velocities] = propagateOrbit(time, a, ecc, incl, RAAN, argp, nu)
[positions, velocities] = propagateOrbit(time, rEpoch, vEpoch)
[___] = propagateOrbit(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: datetime scalar or vector of target times.

tools.notes: Outputs are in meters and m/s (3-by-m-by-numSpacecraft). For visualization and access analysis use satelliteScenario.

tools.name: tleread
tools.description: Reads a two-line element (TLE) file into a structure array of mean orbital elements with epochs, ready for propagateOrbit or satellite scenarios.
tools.usage: tleStruct = tleread(file)

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Path to a .tle or text file with one or more TLE sets.

tools.notes: ommread reads CCSDS orbit mean-elements messages. TLEs use the SGP4 theory; propagate them with SGP4/SDP4 for accuracy.

tools.name: airspeed
tools.description: Computes airspeed (magnitude) from body or wind velocity component arrays.
tools.usage: V = airspeed(velocities)

parameters.name: velocities
parameters.description: m-by-3 array of velocity components [u v w].

tools.notes: Combine with alphabeta, dpressure and machnumber for flight parameter calculations.

tools.name: alphabeta
tools.description: Computes angle of attack and sideslip angle from body-axis velocity components, the fundamental incidence angles in aircraft aerodynamics.
tools.usage: [alpha, beta] = alphabeta(velocities)
tools.notes: Outputs in radians. dcmbody2wind uses these angles to build the body-to-wind transformation.

tools.name: correctairspeed
tools.description: Converts between true airspeed (TAS), equivalent airspeed (EAS) and calibrated airspeed (CAS) given speed of sound and static pressure. Needed when comparing pitot readings with flight dynamics models.
tools.usage: outputAirspeed = correctairspeed(inputAirspeed, speedOfSound, pressure0, inputAirspeedType, outputAirspeedType)

parameters.name: speedOfSound / pressure0
parameters.description: Local speed of sound (m/s) and static pressure (Pa), e.g. from atmosisa.

tools.example:
[~, a, P] = atmosisa(3000);
tas = correctairspeed(120, a, P, "CAS", "TAS")
tools.notes: Valid for subsonic flow up to Mach 1.

tools.name: dpressure
tools.description: Computes dynamic pressure q = 0.5*rho*V^2 from velocity components and air density.
tools.usage: q = dpressure(velocities, rho)
tools.example:
[~, ~, ~, rho] = atmoscoesa(5000);
q = dpressure([150 0 5], rho)     % Pa
tools.notes: Dynamic pressure scales aerodynamic forces: L = q*S*CL.

tools.name: machnumber
tools.description: Computes Mach number from velocity components and the local speed of sound.
tools.usage: mach = machnumber(velocities, speedOfSound)
tools.notes: Use flowisentropic and flownormalshock for compressible flow relations at a given Mach number.

tools.name: flowisentropic
tools.description: Computes isentropic flow relations (Mach number, temperature, pressure, density and area ratios) for a calorically perfect gas, given any one of these quantities.
tools.usage:
[mach, T, P, rho, area] = flowisentropic(gamma, flow)
[mach, T, P, rho, area] = flowisentropic(gamma, flow, mtype)

parameters.name: flow
parameters.description: Input values of the quantity selected by mtype.

tools.example:
[M, T, P, rho, A] = flowisentropic(1.4, 2.0)          % Mach 2
M_exit = flowisentropic(1.4, 4.0, "sup")              % nozzle area ratio 4
tools.notes: Ratios are static-to-total (T/T0, P/P0, rho/rho0) and A/A*. Related: flownormalshock, flowprandtlmeyer, flowrayleigh, flowfanno.

tools.name: flownormalshock
tools.description: Computes normal shock relations: upstream and downstream Mach numbers, and static temperature, pressure, density and total pressure ratios across the shock, given any one of them.
tools.usage:
[mach, T, P, rho, downstream_mach, P0, P1] = flownormalshock(gamma, normal_shock_relations)
[___] = flownormalshock(gamma, normal_shock_relations, mtype)
tools.example: [M1, T21, P21, rho21, M2, P0ratio] = flownormalshock(1.4, 2.5)
tools.notes: Upstream Mach must be > 1. Use the "pitot" type to infer supersonic Mach from Rayleigh pitot readings.

tools.name: convlength
tools.description: Converts length values between aerospace-relevant units (ft, m, km, in, mi, naut mi). Part of a family of conversion utilities for velocity, mass, force, pressure, temperature, angle and more.
tools.usage: convertedValues = convlength(valuesToConvert, inputUnits, outputUnits)
tools.notes: Family: convacc, convang, convangacc, convangvel, convdensity, convforce, convmass, convpres, convtemp, convvel.

tools.name: juliandate
tools.description: Computes the Julian date for calendar dates and times, a common time base for ephemerides, orbit propagation and astronomical calculations.
tools.usage:
jd = juliandate(v)
jd = juliandate(y, mo, d)
jd = juliandate(y, mo, d, h, mi, s)

parameters.name: y, mo, d, h, mi, s
parameters.description: Year, month, day, hour, minute, second.

tools.notes: Related: mjuliandate, decyear, leapyear, tdbjuliandate, siderealTime. Base MATLAB also provides juliandate(t) for datetime arrays.

tools.name: fixedWingAircraft
tools.description: Creates an Aero.FixedWing aircraft object with name, reference area, span and chord, and a chosen degrees-of-freedom model. It is the entry point of the fixed-wing modeling workflow (coefficients, surfaces, thrust, states, stability analysis).
tools.usage:
aircraft = fixedWingAircraft(name)
aircraft = fixedWingAircraft(name, referencearea, referencespan, referencelength)
aircraft = fixedWingAircraft(___, degreesoffreedom)
aircraft = fixedWingAircraft(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: referencearea / referencespan / referencelength
parameters.description: Wing area S, span b and mean aerodynamic chord c.

tools.notes: Introduced R2021b. Related: fixedWingState, fixedWingCoefficient, fixedWingSurface, fixedWingThrust, aircraftEnvironment. Aero.FixedWing methods include staticStability, linearize and nonlinearDynamics; datcomToFixedWing and jsbsimToFixedWing import existing data.

tools.name: Aero.Animation
tools.description: Creates a MATLAB-figure-based 3-D animation object that plays back vehicle position and attitude time histories using body geometry files (e.g. AC3D, MAT), with camera control and optional video recording.
tools.usage:
h = Aero.Animation
idx = createBody(h, geometryFile, geometryFormat)
show(h); play(h)

parameters.name: Bodies{idx}.TimeSeriesSourceType
parameters.description: E.g. "Array6DoF" ([t x y z phi theta psi]), "Timeseries", "StructureWithTime".

parameters.name: VideoRecord / VideoFileName
parameters.description: Record the animation to a video file.

tools.notes: Aero.Body, Aero.Camera and Aero.Geometry are the component classes. For FlightGear visualization use Aero.FlightGearAnimation.

tools.name: datcomimport
tools.description: Imports aerodynamic coefficient data from USAF Digital DATCOM output files into MATLAB structures, which can then populate aircraft models (e.g. via datcomToFixedWing or Simulink lookup tables).
tools.usage:
aero = datcomimport(file)
aero = datcomimport(file, usenan, verbose, filetype)

parameters.name: usenan
parameters.description: true (default) to fill missing data with NaN instead of zeros.

tools.notes: Returns a cell array with one structure per DATCOM case; field names follow DATCOM coefficient names (cd, cl, cm, cyb...).
